guide:
How to play
The steps
Create your player: name, one of 50 nationalities, one of 10 positions, and a starting era from the 1990s to the 2020s.
Build your look in the appearance editor: 12 skin tones, 29 hairstyles, 16 hair colours, 18 beard styles, 16 accessories, 18 boot lines, and 19 signature celebrations, or hit Surprise me.
Roll your starting potential, somewhere in the mid 50s to high 60s, and reroll as many times as you like. Rerolls are free and there is no limit on them.
Open Customize your build to set your starting overall anywhere from 40 to 99, move points between the six attribute families, shape the specifics under each family, and set your height and weight.
Begin in an academy matched to your nationality and talent. Pro contract offers arrive from age 17.
Advance season by season through simulated stats, newspaper headlines, random events, and decisions.
Most summers open with one card about your position or your career, before the rest of the news between seasons. Training can trade one skill for another next season, with gains stopping at your ceiling.
Want to see it happen? The 📺 Week by week button plays the same season match by match, with your rating every game and the league table after every matchday, then hands you back to the newspaper. Its ? button has the rules and worked examples.
Up to three times a season the clock stops and the moment is yours to play on your training ground board (look for 🎯 on the fixtures): a YOUR CALL decides how that match went, with the return game taking the other side so your final table and season totals never move, and a RECREATE replays what the record says you did, for stars that bank into next season's growth.
Open the training ground (the dumbbell button, above your player on phones or bottom right on desktop) once a season. Your position picks a drill you actually play: keepers hold and drag a glove save dive, centre backs, full backs and defensive midfielders time a tackle on a moving ball, central and attacking midfielders thread a through ball onto a runner before he is offside, and everyone else times a wall shot through a gap that opens and closes. Today's ten rounds are the same for everyone at your position and count once; practice is unlimited and banks nothing.
Work the transfer windows: stay, extend, request a move, or weigh rival offers and dream club pay cuts.
When the window offers it, open Set transfer priority, choose minutes, club level or home country, save the brief, then use Request transfer. Saving the brief alone does not request a move, and No Agent can use it too.
After a settled senior season, open Review representation to compare agent terms or choose No Agent before a later deal.
Spend the money in 8 shop aisles: property, vehicles, investments, lifestyle, performance, flex, family, and a shady aisle that only appears once you have something to hide.
Retire, on your terms or your body's, collect the legacy verdict, then carry on as a manager, pundit, or owner if you want.
Want one last year? Eligible players from 30 can open Plan a farewell season, read the terms and confirm their final year. You can still choose to retire immediately.
If you previously retired from internationals, an eligible National-team comeback lets you make yourself available again after a settled season.
The rules
Stats grow slowly and honestly: 1 to 3 points a year through the academy and your prime, less once you pass 86, and barely at all above 90. Reaching world class is a decade of work, not three good seasons.
Growth fades once your hidden prime type (early, normal, late, or extended) ends, with decline turning brutal from 38.
The club that raised you always offers you a first team deal when you turn pro, so you can spend a whole career at your boyhood club, and it can call you home again from 27.
Retirement is suggested from age 30 once you drop 10 off your peak or hit 75 overall, forced below 50 overall at 33 or older, and automatic at 45.
From 30, renewal and transfer pay follow your age, overall and latest playing season. A renewal or extension lasts two years at 30 to 33, then one from 34. Another club keeps the years shown on its offer.
A money talk still has a 50% chance of success. From 30, success raises or holds your current wage; it does not renew the contract.
A farewell is one declared final year for eligible players aged 30 to 44. The announcement is saved and cannot be undone or extended. Finish its results and queued ceremonies, then retire. Injuries, bans and forced retirement still apply; appearances and trophies are not promised.
The World Cup comes every 4 years. Top nations qualify about 90 percent of the time, while a small nation mostly needs a world class you.
After international retirement, eligible players aged 18 to 44 with a recorded cap can return once per recorded season. Existing caps, goals, trophies and history stay the same. Returning opens selection, not an instant call-up or extra caps; injury, bans and failed qualification can still keep you out.
Legacy runs 0 to 100: 90 is GOAT, 80 LEGEND, 70 GREAT, 60 SOLID PRO, and less is JOURNEYMAN. The verdict also knows the overall you started at, so climbing from 54 to 91 scores better than being handed 91 on the creation screen.
There is no cap on your starting overall, but a high start eats the room you had to grow into, and if you are already world class as a teenager you pick up far more injuries before you turn 24.
Your ceiling is not welded shut. Two seasons in a row that are both elite and decorated, while you are already pressed against it, buy one point back at a time. 99 is the hard wall and nothing gets past it.
A position drill is ten rounds and its session score is wins times ten. 50 pays +1 to the drill's attribute with next season's growth (shooting for the wall shot, defending for the tackle, passing for the through ball, reflexes for the glove save) and 80 pays +2, capped at the room between your overall and your ceiling, so a drill never lifts you past it. It shares the one training session a season with the cone slalom, sprint burst, passing gates and penalty sessions.
Height and weight are real numbers, not decoration: a tall heavy player wins more in the air and is stronger, and is slower off the mark and less agile for it.
Morale runs 0 to 100, moves with events and choices, and counts: 89 and up adds a league game and a tenth on your rating, 73 and under costs the same, 58 and under two of each, never more than three games together with the dressing room. Scandals feed an integrity ledger worth minus 30 to plus 20 legacy points at the end.
A statistically dominant season cannot be snubbed at the Ballon d'Or. Outscore the whole shortlist while winning a major and the trophy is yours, and any 45 goal or 55 goal involvement season finishes on the podium at worst.
After a settled senior season, ages 19 to 44 can change representation once per recorded season. Agents and No Agent affect future signings and income fees; your current wage, savings and already-paid fees stay the same.
A transfer priority searches the clubs already eligible for your age and rating. The usual response chance is 50%; a broken appearance promise guarantees a response, but not an offer. The response is saved for that window and cannot be rerolled by reloading. Projected minutes are not guaranteed starts, and club-arranged sales and loans keep their own flow.
Corruption heat runs 0 to 100 and cools 8 a year when you stay clean. Past 70 the financial crimes unit can raid you, and past 90 comes a conviction, seized money, and a season in prison that wrecks your stats.
Unexplained money keeps generating heat every season until you wash it through a shady business or declare it and eat the tax.
Derbies: if your club has a real rival in the same league, you meet them twice a season in the league. We only count a rivalry two separate sources back, in leagues and years where we checked how often the clubs meet, so some clubs have none yet.
You play the derbies you are picked for, roughly in line with your league appearances. Each one you win adds 2 popularity and 2 morale, each one you lose takes 2 off both, a draw changes nothing, the swing is capped every season and your rating is never touched.
Score the goal that puts you ahead for good in a derby win and the season counts as a Derby Hero season, worth 2 more popularity. Example: at Arsenal you beat Tottenham 2-1 at home with the winner and draw 1-1 away, so that is +4 popularity, +2 morale and a Derby Hero.
Every season your club plays its country's domestic cup as a run, from the early rounds to the final, and the cup carries its real name (the FA Cup, the Copa del Rey, the DFB-Pokal) wherever two sources back it; a cup that was not played that season cannot be won.
Go out early and your season summary names the round and the club that knocked you out. Win it and the celebration walks you through the run, and your trophy chip names the cup.
Recent club form: last season at the same club needs 10 to 38 recorded league appearances. A rating of 7.6 or more adds two to next year's selection draw; 6.4 or less takes two away. Phone effects and frozen-out limits still apply. Example: a 24-game draw becomes 26 after a qualifying 7.8 season.
Preseason plan: choose development (+1 position skill after growth, 3 percentage points more injury risk), recovery (-1 skill, 4 points less risk), or balanced. Example: 20% injury risk becomes 23% or 16%, within existing limits. A serious injury or no appearances interrupts development; a move cancels the plan.
Academy mentoring: the Youth Mentor event starts one generated player. Ten senior appearances at your shared club adds one mentoring year. Example: 12 appearances moves 0/3 to 1/3; six appearances pauses it. Three qualifying years complete it, a move ends it, and its history stays in the mentor tile.
Phone and Training sit above your player on a phone. Career Story opens your saved chapters; Previous and Next move between them, and All seasons returns to the tile you opened.
Accepting a smaller role from a new manager means 4 fewer planned league games next season at that club. It lasts one recorded season; a move, loan or retirement clears it. Example: a selection of 30 becomes 26 before existing selection limits, injuries and bans.
Personal goal milestones count the goals of your recorded senior club seasons, excluding academy and international goals. Example: 99 senior club goals plus 2 this season takes you past 100, with a new total of 101. The summary shows that crossing.
Summer cards: most summers open with one card about your position or your career. Training on it gives a skill +1 and another -1 next season, since the hours come from your normal work, never past your ceiling. Example: penalty duty for a striker is Shooting +1, Dribbling -1.
One tab at a time: the career plays in the newest tab you opened. An older tab asks you to reload. Example: open it in two tabs and play a season in the second; the first asks you to reload, and the reload shows that season.
A worked example

Take a Nigerian striker rolled at 63, a Gifted start. Two academy years push him past 70, and at 18 a bidding war breaks out. He takes minutes over money, bags 20 league goals, and the papers crown him the next superstar.

At 22 a dream club calls with a pay cut, and he signs anyway. A league title lands in year two, then a torn hamstring eats half a season, and a moral dilemma offers a shady shortcut back to fitness. He refuses, banking integrity, while the rival the game spawned at his debut, a preening Brazilian winger, lifts the Ballon d'Or. The snub becomes fuel.

A separate pay example: with No Agent, at 35 and 76 overall after a playing season rated 7.1, a €1,000 base offer is quoted at €850 a week. Another club keeps the years shown on its offer. If the current wage is €1,000, a successful pay talk holds it at €1,000 instead of cutting it, without renewing the contract.

The revenge arc peaks at 26: a Champions League, a World Cup semifinal carrying Nigeria, then the Ballon d'Or, where he thanks the rival from the stage. An extended prime runs to 36, the fortune buys his boyhood club, and he retires at 38 with a legacy of 84, LEGEND tier, one Champions League short of GOAT talk.
